title: Section 117 after-care
blurb: Identify who is entitled to s117 after-care, who must provide it, and when it can lawfully end.
question: Mr Osei is about to leave hospital after 5 months on section 3. He is worried about paying for the supported accommodation the team recommends. His neighbour on the ward, who was on section 2, asks whether she gets the same help. What should the nurse explain?

teach.h: A legal duty to support recovery
teach.body: Section 117 places a joint duty on the integrated care board (ICB) and the local social services authority to provide or arrange after-care for people who have been detained for treatment and then leave hospital. After-care means services that meet needs arising from or related to the mental disorder and reduce the risk of the person's condition worsening and readmission. In plain English: if the law kept you in hospital for treatment, the state must help you stay well afterwards.

rows.label: Informal
values: After s3, if stayed on informally

teach.caption: Entitlement includes s3 patients on s17 leave or a CTO, people of any age, and those who stayed in hospital informally before leaving (COP15 33.2, 33.9).

items.label: bodies share the duty: ICB and local authority
after-care cannot end while on a CTO

teach.caption: Care and Support Statutory Guidance: s117 after-care is provided free of charge.
Read broadly: any service meeting a need arising from or related to the disorder.

children.edge: Reason is discharge from CMHT, time passed, or readmitted on s2
children.label: Not a lawful reason alone

children.edge: ICB and LA both satisfied no longer needed
children.label: May end
children.sub: Involve the person, carer and advocate

teach.caption: COP15 33.20-33.21. After-care can be reinstated if withdrawn too early (33.22).

items: Identify on admission whether the person will be entitled to s117 and start after-care planning early (COP15 33.10).
Make sure the RC considers after-care needs before leave of more than a short period, discharge or a CTO (33.13).
Involve the person, carers and the wider team; record what is provided under s117 (33.14-33.15).
Explain the person can decline services, and can still receive them later if they change their mind (33.24).

teach.h: Scenario: Mr Osei and his neighbour
teach.body: Mr Osei was detained under s3, so he is entitled to s117 after-care from the ICB and local authority jointly. Supported accommodation that meets a need arising from his mental disorder can be part of it, free of charge. His neighbour was on s2, which is not listed in s117(1), so she has no s117 entitlement; she can still receive care planned under normal NHS and Care Act routes. The nurse records the conversation and links both to their care coordinators.

teach.text: Section 2 does NOT give s117 entitlement, even though it is a detention. And after-care must not be withdrawn just because the person was discharged from specialist services, an arbitrary time has passed, they returned to hospital informally or on s2, or their CTO or leave ended (COP15 33.21).

items: Entitled: s3, s37, s45A, s47, s48 patients who cease to be detained and leave hospital.
Not entitled: s2, s4, s5, s135, s136 alone.
Joint, free duty on the ICB and local social services authority until both agree it is no longer needed.
Cannot end while on a CTO; plan from admission; the person may decline and still return to it.

summary: You can now identify who is entitled to s117 after-care, who must provide it and what it can include. You can also explain when after-care may lawfully end and which reasons are not enough.

A.q: Which patient is entitled to section 117 after-care on leaving hospital?
options: A patient discharged from section 2
A patient discharged from section 3
A patient released from section 136
A patient held under section 5(2)
A.why: Section 117(1) applies to people detained under s3 (and s37, s45A, s47, s48) who then cease to be detained and leave hospital.

whyNot.0: Section 2 is not listed in s117(1).
whyNot.2: Place-of-safety detention under s136 does not create entitlement.
whyNot.3: The s5(2) holding power is not a s117 qualifying section.

A.q: Which bodies share the statutory duty to provide section 117 after-care in England?
options: The ICB and the local social services authority
The hospital managers and the patient's GP practice
The local authority and the probation service
The NHS trust and the Care Quality Commission
A.why: Section 117(2): the duty falls jointly on the integrated care board and the local social services authority, in co-operation with voluntary agencies.

whyNot.1: Neither hospital managers nor GP practices hold the s117 duty.
whyNot.2: Probation is not a s117 body.
whyNot.3: The CQC regulates; it does not provide after-care.

A.q: A patient asks whether they will have to pay for their section 117 after-care services. What is accurate?
options: They pay a means-tested contribution
They pay for the accommodation part
They pay after the first 6 weeks
The services are free of charge
A.why: Care and Support Statutory Guidance: s117 after-care is provided free of charge and is excluded from local authority charging.

whyNot.0: Means-tested charging applies to Care Act services, not s117 after-care.
whyNot.1: Accommodation provided as after-care is free; a top-up can be paid only for a more expensive preferred choice.
whyNot.2: There is no 6-week cut-off for free after-care.

B.q: Mr Patel is on a community treatment order. His local authority proposes ending his section 117 after-care because he has been stable for a year. What is the correct position?
options: It can end with the ICB's agreement
It can end after 12 months of stability
It cannot end while he is on a CTO
It can end if he gives written consent
B.why: Section 117(2): the ICB and local authority cannot be satisfied that after-care is no longer needed while the person remains a community patient.

whyNot.0: Even joint agreement cannot end after-care during a CTO.
whyNot.1: An arbitrary period is not a lawful reason (COP15 33.21).
whyNot.3: He may decline services, but the duty itself cannot end while he is on a CTO.

B.q: When should planning for section 117 after-care begin?
options: On the day of discharge
As soon as the patient is admitted
At the first tribunal hearing
When section 17 leave is first granted
B.why: COP15 33.10: the duty starts when the person leaves hospital, but planning should start as soon as they are admitted.

whyNot.0: Waiting until discharge risks the person leaving without services.
whyNot.2: Tribunals expect after-care information, but planning should already be under way.
whyNot.3: Before leave the RC must check after-care needs, but planning starts earlier.

B.q: Ms Jordan, previously on section 3 and now receiving after-care, is readmitted under section 2. The local authority suggests stopping her section 117 services. What does the Code say?
options: Readmission on s2 is not a reason on its own
Readmission ends entitlement to s117
Section 2 replaces s117 with s2 after-care
She must be detained under s3 again to receive after-care
B.why: COP15 33.21: after-care should not be withdrawn solely because the person has returned to hospital informally or under s2.

whyNot.1: Readmission does not end the duty.
whyNot.2: Section 2 carries no after-care duty of its own.
whyNot.3: Her existing entitlement continues; a new s3 is not needed.

C.q: Kai, 17, leaves hospital after 4 months on section 3. His plan includes supported accommodation and a college mentoring scheme linked to his recovery. Which statement is correct?
options: s117 does not apply to under-18s
Accommodation is charged under the Care Act
College support is outside s117
Both can be s117 after-care, free of charge
C.why: s117 applies at any age (COP15 33.2) and is read broadly: housing and education or employment support meeting needs related to the disorder can be after-care (33.4), free of charge.

whyNot.0: The Code states s117 applies to people of all ages, including children.
whyNot.1: Accommodation provided as s117 after-care is not charged.
whyNot.2: Services meeting wider needs related to the disorder can be after-care.

C.q: After discharge from section 3, Mr Osei declines the after-care offered. Six months later his mood worsens and he asks for support. What is the position?
options: He lost entitlement by declining
He must be detained again to qualify
He can still receive it under s117
He must pay as he declined it at first
C.why: COP15 33.24: patients may decline after-care, but this does not stop them receiving services under s117 if they change their mind.

whyNot.0: Declining does not end the duty or the entitlement.
whyNot.1: A new detention is not required.

C.q: The community team discharges Ms Rees from specialist mental health services. She still lives in supported housing provided under section 117. Which action is most appropriate?
options: End s117 as specialist care has ended
Ask her GP to take over the funding
Transfer her housing to Care Act charging
Review jointly whether needs remain first
C.why: After-care ends only when the ICB and local authority are both satisfied it is no longer needed; discharge from specialist services alone is not a reason (COP15 33.20-33.21), and new arrangements must be in place first.

whyNot.0: Discharge from specialist services is listed as not a reason on its own.
whyNot.1: GPs do not hold the s117 duty.
whyNot.2: Moving to charged care without ending s117 lawfully would breach the duty.

reteach.title: Treatment detention earns after-care
reteach.question: How can you remember who gets s117?

blocks.body: Ask: was the person detained for treatment? Section 3 and the court and prison transfer orders (s37, s45A, s47, s48) are treatment detentions, so they earn after-care. Assessment (s2), emergency (s4), holding (s5) and police powers (s135, s136) do not. Once earned, after-care is free and lasts until the ICB and local authority both agree it is no longer needed.

steps.label: Joint review
steps.sub: Ends only when no longer needed

blocks.text: Section 2 is a detention but not a treatment detention: no s117.

explain.body: s117 applies to people detained under s3, s37, s45A, s47 or s48 who cease to be detained and leave hospital, whether or not immediately. It includes those on s17 leave or a CTO.

test.q: Which order gives entitlement to section 117 after-care?
options: A section 37 hospital order
A section 135 warrant
A section 4 emergency admission
A section 5(4) holding power
test.why: Section 37 hospital orders are listed in s117(1).

whyNot.2: Section 4 is an emergency assessment route.
whyNot.3: Section 5(4) is a nurse's holding power.

explain.body: The ICB and the local social services authority jointly provide or arrange after-care, in co-operation with voluntary agencies. It is free of charge.

test.q: Which statement about the section 117 duty is correct?
options: It falls on the detaining hospital
It is shared by the ICB and local authority
It is means-tested by the local authority each year
It lasts a maximum of 12 months
test.why: Section 117(2) places the duty jointly on the ICB and local social services authority; it is free and has no fixed time limit.

whyNot.0: The hospital plans discharge but does not hold the s117 duty.

explain.body: Only when the ICB and local authority are both satisfied it is no longer needed, and not while the person is on a CTO. Not solely because of discharge from specialist services, time passed, readmission, a DoLS, or the end of a CTO or leave.

test.q: Which is a lawful basis for ending section 117 after-care?
options: The person's CTO has just ended
Two years have passed since discharge from hospital
Both bodies are satisfied it is no longer needed
The person moved to a different town
test.why: Section 117(2): the duty continues until both the ICB and local authority are satisfied the person no longer needs after-care.

whyNot.0: The end of a CTO alone is not a reason (COP15 33.21).
whyNot.1: An arbitrary period is not a reason.
whyNot.3: Moving changes who arranges care, not whether the duty exists.

explain.body: People can decline after-care, and decisions should be fully informed. Declining does not end entitlement: services can start later. Services withdrawn too early can be reinstated.

test.q: What happens if a person entitled to section 117 declines the after-care offered?
options: Entitlement ends on the day they decline
They must sign a waiver for 12 months
They are referred to the tribunal
They can still accept services later
test.why: COP15 33.24: declining should not prevent the person receiving s117 services if they change their mind.

whyNot.2: Declining after-care has no tribunal consequence.
